active_paradigms.idea: Exploit symmetry: optimize in the fundamental domain under the 3-fold dihedral group D3 with points forced onto symmetry orbits (vertices, edge-midpoints, or orbits of size 3/6), reducing the search dimension drastically and letting a hard-max LP-style solver find exact symmetric optima.
active_paradigms.description: Known good Heilbronn configurations for n=11 in an equilateral triangle are highly symmetric. Parameterize the configuration as: 3 vertices, plus orbits under the 120° rotation/reflection group. E.g., place k points on each edge at equal arc positions and one center point, then optimize only 1-3 free scalar parameters (edge fractions, interior orbit radius). With so few parameters, do a dense grid scan followed by scipy.optimize.minimize (Nelder-Mead or SLSQP) on the exact min-area function (computed via the 165-triangle vectorized numpy min). Because the parameter space is tiny, you can afford extremely fine multi-start and even a brute-force sweep, reliably finding the global optimum within symmetric families. Also try the C3-symmetric family with orbits of size 3 at barycentric (a,b,c) and rotations, plus orbits of size 6. This converts a 22-dim nonconvex problem into a handful of 1-3 dim scans that can be solved to machine precision.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized (primary), eval_time (tiny parameter space makes it fast)
active_paradigms.cautions: Symmetric configs can have degenerate collinear triples giving zero area; verify the min over all 165 triplets explicitly. Keep the exact min-area evaluation (not softmin) since the parameter count is small; use tolerance 1e-6 for boundary containment.

active_paradigms.idea: Hard-max via sequential linear programming (LP-based maximin): iteratively solve a linear program that raises a uniform lower bound t on all triangle areas, using signed-area linearization around the current configuration.
active_paradigms.description: The maximin problem max min_i area_i is a hard-max problem that can be attacked with the classic LP approach: at each iteration, fix a sign assignment sigma_i (orientation of each triplet) from the current iterate, then the constraint area_i >= t is linear in the point coordinates; solve the resulting LP with scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS) to maximize t subject to triangle-containment linear constraints and signed-area >= t for all 165 triplets. If the LP is infeasible or the true min-area drops (wrong sign guesses), flip signs of violated triplets and re-solve. Iterate until signs stabilize — this converges to a local optimum of the hard-max problem far more precisely than softmin annealing, and often jumps to better local optima because LP steps are globally optimal within the linearization. Warm-start from the current program's best configuration and from several symmetric starts.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized — squeezes the exact maximin value beyond what softmin+polish achieves
active_paradigms.cautions: Sign (orientation) patterns must be consistent; if a triplet becomes collinear the LP can become degenerate — add small regularization or skip re-linearization for near-zero-area triplets. Containment constraints are simple linear bounds on barycentric coordinates. Use scipy.optimize.linprog with method='highs' for speed and reliability.

active_paradigms.idea: Simulated annealing / basin-hopping on the exact min-area with a dedicated move set (point insertion along Voronoi-like 'safe' directions), implemented via scipy.optimize.basinhopping with a custom step class, seeded from many structured starts.
active_paradigms.description: Replace the softmin L-BFGS pipeline with scipy.optimize.basinhopping operating directly on -min_area (exact, vectorized over 165 triplets) with a custom take_step that proposes structured moves: move the vertex of the currently smallest triangle along the direction that increases its area (perpendicular to the opposite side), snap random points to the boundary (boundary-heavy configs are known to be good for n=11), and apply small Dirichlet-resampled perturbations. The accept/reject at the Metropolis level lets the search cross barriers between local optima that hill-climbing polish cannot, while the local minimizer (L-BFGS on softmin with tiny temperature, reused from current code) refines each basin. Run many short basinhopping chains with a fixed seed within the time budget, keep the best exact min-area ever seen, and finish with the existing polish routine.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized via better global exploration; eval_time kept in check by budgeting iterations
active_paradigms.cautions: Determinism: pass a seeded np.random.Generator into the step class and to basinhopping's seed argument. Ensure every proposed point stays inside the triangle (clip barycentric coordinates and renormalize). The exact min-area objective is piecewise-smooth; use the softmin local minimizer with small temperature (e.g., 1e-5) as the inner 'minimize' to keep gradients well-defined.
